scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 9 · Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, drinking-water safety assessment, purification certification, laboratory safety certification or permission for hazardous heating, chemical handling, dust generation, ingestion or powered-device experiments.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 9 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion while preserving separation-versus-purity/potability limits and the no-tasting, no-unknown-chemical, no-dust-inhalation, no-improvised-powered-device, no-hazardous-heating and no-ingestion boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner chooses a separation method from habit or appearance without identifying which observable property differs between the mixture components.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use supplied mixture cards to name the components, identify one relevant property difference such as particle size, visibility, settling, solubility or state, and then select a matching separation method without handling unknown materials.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: For unfamiliar low-risk or diagrammed mixtures, consistently states the component/property evidence before selecting a separation method and rejects methods that do not use the relevant property difference.

scenarios.need: Learner expects ordinary filtration to remove a dissolved substance such as salt simply because the liquid passes through a filter.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied diagrams of an insoluble solid suspension and a dissolved-solid solution, predict what ordinary filter paper can retain, and explain why dissolved particles are not removed by the same classroom filtration step.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly distinguishes insoluble-particle filtration from dissolved-solute separation and explains the method limit without claiming that filtration makes the liquid pure or safe to drink.

scenarios.need: Learner sees a clear filtered or decanted liquid and concludes that it must be pure, disinfected and safe to drink.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Analyse supplied before/after separation evidence and list what the chosen method can remove, what it may leave behind and what additional evidence would be needed before any purity, disinfection or potability claim; do not drink any test sample.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: States that visual clarity alone does not establish purity, disinfection or potability and limits conclusions to the particles or components the demonstrated method is capable of separating.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes dusty winnowing with an improvised powered fan or mechanical device to make the separation more dramatic.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the dusty powered demonstration and instead use supplied diagrams or sealed/clean classroom evidence to explain how a moving-air method can separate components with different effective weight or aerodynamic behaviour.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies inhalation, eye and improvised-device hazards, chooses a non-dusty evidence source and still explains the physical property difference used by winnowing.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes a flame, kettle, hot plate, oven, microwave, improvised electrical heater or sealed-container heating to evaporate a solution independently.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the hazardous heating plan and use supplied process diagrams, data or an adult-prepared example to reason conceptually about evaporation and recovery of a non-volatile dissolved solid without operating a heat source.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Recognises the named heating and pressure hazards, selects a safer evidence source and correctly describes which component can be recovered conceptually through evaporation without instructing learner-operated heating.

scenarios.need: Learner loses track of mixture components in a multi-step separation and assumes each step removes every unwanted substance.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Trace each component through a supplied multi-step flow diagram, recording what is retained, transferred or still dissolved after each stage and identifying why a second method may be needed.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Accurately tracks all components through an unfamiliar separation sequence, states the limitation of each step and selects the next method from the remaining component properties.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes a recovered solid or separated liquid is automatically chemically pure because it has been isolated from one other component.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Inspect supplied separation evidence and distinguish 'recovered from this mixture' from 'proven chemically pure', naming at least one possible remaining impurity or missing test without performing chemical testing.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses evidence-limited language, avoids purity overclaims and explains that successful separation from one component does not by itself establish complete chemical purity.

scenarios.need: Learner needs offline separation practice without uploading photos/location, tasting samples, handling unknown chemicals, generating dust or using powered/heated apparatus.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Complete cached text, diagrams and supplied mixture cards locally to choose separation methods, identify method limits and sequence safe steps without sensors, uploads, ingestion, unknown substances, dust generation, powered devices or heat sources.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline synthetic task using supplied evidence only, selects defensible separation methods, states purity/potability limits and avoids personal-data disclosure and hazardous physical experimentation.
